t: Historian: spoke memory advisor — session history ingestion, deferred work detection, spec validation

content.what: A spoke advisor that owns session memory. Ingests WAI track files and WAI-Lugs.jsonl to answer: what was discussed, what was incompletely implemented, what was skipped and why. Supplies historical context to Lug Advisor and QA Guardian on demand. Validates that specifications still match implementation.
content.why: Every session currently starts cold. Lug Advisor and QA Guardian explicitly depend on Historian for deferred/incomplete work and spec validation. Without it, context continuity — a core WAI value — is absent. Historian is the prerequisite for the other advisor lugs in this batch.

process: Index all track files by session_id and timestamp
Detect incomplete work: lugs opened but not closed, tasks mentioned not captured
Detect skipped work: items deferred with reason, explicitly punted
On query from Lug Advisor: return list of deferred/incomplete items with context
On query from QA Guardian: return spec snapshot for given lug/feature
Validate current implementation against stored spec — surface mismatches
behavior_specification.outputs: Structured context responses to advisor queries; optional summary surface at wakeup

constraints: Read-only — never modifies track files or lugs
Must handle missing or partial track data gracefully (not all sessions have tracks)
Performance: index lazily, do not load all tracks on every wakeup
No separate storage — derives from existing WAI files only
acceptance_criteria: Lug Advisor can query Historian and receive list of deferred/incomplete items
QA Guardian can query Historian and receive spec snapshot for a given lug
Wakeup shows 'Historian: N incomplete, M deferred' summary line
Handles spoke with zero track files without error
dependencies: WAI track files present in WAI-Spoke/sessions/

t: Lug Advisor: drive open lugs to ready-to-implement state, supply spoke action roadmap

content.what: A spoke advisor with a focused mission to get open lugs to 'ready to implement' state. Works in three layers: (1) landed open lugs in the spoke — assess readiness, fill gaps, add acceptance_criteria and estimated_steps; (2) consults Historian for work discussed but incompletely implemented or skipped; (3) collaborates with other spokes in the same team to solicit shared work.
content.why: Without this advisor, spoke action roadmaps require manual triage. Lugs land without acceptance criteria, missing scopes, or blocked dependencies. This advisor is the engine that converts inbox ideas and signals into actionable, sequenced work.

behavior_specification.inputs: WAI-Spoke/WAI-Lugs.jsonl (open lugs), Historian query responses, team spoke registry
process: Scan all open lugs: classify as ready / needs_refinement / blocked
For needs_refinement: identify missing fields (acceptance_criteria, estimated_steps, scope, constraints)
Query Historian for deferred/incomplete work not currently in lug list
For each deferred item: surface as candidate lug with source context
Optionally query team spokes for shared or related open lugs
Present prioritized roadmap: ready → needs_refinement → blocked → deferred candidates
behavior_specification.outputs: Prioritized spoke action roadmap; per-lug readiness report; list of Historian-sourced candidates

constraints: Reads from WAI-Lugs.jsonl and Historian — does not auto-create lugs without confirmation
Historian must be available for deferred work detection (degrades gracefully without it)
Team spoke collaboration is advisory — does not pull work from other spokes without confirmation
acceptance_criteria: Running /wai-lug-advisor produces a prioritized roadmap from current open lugs
Each lug classified as ready / needs_refinement / blocked with reason
Historian-sourced deferred items surface as candidates with original context
At least one 'needs_refinement' lug gets its gaps filled in a session

t: Automated Changelog from Lugs: man-page style entries, lug-traceable, UAT checklist per entry

content.what: Automatically generate a structured changelog entry when a lug is completed. Each entry follows a man-page inspired format: Problem / Solution / Lug Ref / UAT Checklist. Entries are grouped per project with a running index. Manual changelog entries are excluded — only lug-driven entries.
content.why: Users and testers need to understand what changed and why with each deployment. Currently there is no structured record linking deployed changes back to their originating lugs. A lug-traceable changelog enables logical UAT: each entry comes with its own test checklist derived from the lug's acceptance criteria.

behavior_specification.inputs: Completed lug (ty=task/feature/epic, s=c), lug acceptance_criteria, lug title and content
process: On lug completion (s → c): extract title, goal, scope, acceptance_criteria
Generate changelog entry: Problem (why it was needed), Solution (what was done), Lug Ref (lug id), UAT (acceptance_criteria as checklist)
Append to per-project CHANGELOG.jsonl
Optionally render as human-readable CHANGELOG.md
behavior_specification.outputs: CHANGELOG.jsonl (machine-readable, append-only), CHANGELOG.md (rendered, overwritten on each lug completion)

content.scope: Lug completion hook. Changelog entry generation. Per-project CHANGELOG.jsonl and CHANGELOG.md. UAT checklist derived from acceptance_criteria.
constraints: Only fires on lug completion — no manual entries

CHANGELOG.jsonl is append-only — never modified retroactively
acceptance_criteria: Completing a lug with acceptance_criteria produces a changelog entry
Entry includes: problem statement, solution summary, lug ref, UAT checklist from acceptance_criteria
CHANGELOG.md renders all entries in human-readable man-page style
Per-project index lists entries with date and lug ref

t: QA Guardian: spoke advisor owning test coverage, closeout quality gates, and production release validation

content.what: A spoke advisor that owns quality as a first-class concern. Responsibilities: (1) owns and maintains the closeout quality gates — not fixed scripts but a living advisor that knows what the gates cover and why; (2) runs extensive tests before production releases using Haiku sub-agents for cost-effective coverage; (3) tracks e2e run history so it always knows the current coverage state; (4) has the prerogative to block a release if gates fail; (5) consults Historian to validate that specifications still match implementation before signing off.
content.why: QA responsibilities currently live in fixed scripts that no one maintains proactively. Coverage gaps go unnoticed. The closeout quality gates exist but have no owner. This advisor elevates quality into a first-class concern — it knows coverage gaps, owns the gates, and has authority to test everything before it reaches the user. It is as important as Historian: it validates specifications and ensures continuity until a lug explicitly changes behavior.

behavior_specification.inputs: Test suite (tests/), closeout event, production release event, Historian spec snapshots, WAI-Lugs.jsonl (completed lugs)
process: On closeout: run spot-check suite; report pass/fail with gap analysis
On production release: orchestrate full test suite via Haiku sub-agents; block release on failure
Track e2e run history in qa-history.jsonl (date, result, coverage %, gaps)
Query Historian for spec snapshot of each completed lug; validate implementation matches spec
Surface coverage gaps proactively at session start if last run was >N days ago
behavior_specification.outputs: Closeout quality gate result (pass/fail + gaps); release validation report; qa-history.jsonl entry; spec validation diff

constraints: Must integrate with existing closeout protocol — quality gates already exist, this advisor owns them
Uses Haiku sub-agents for production release testing — not full Sonnet/Opus to control cost
Must not block development flow — spot checks on closeout, full suite on release only
Read-only on Historian — does not modify specs, only validates against them
acceptance_criteria: Closeout runs QA Guardian spot-check and surfaces pass/fail before commit
Production release triggers full suite via Haiku sub-agent and blocks on failure
qa-history.jsonl accumulates run records with date, result, coverage metrics
QA Guardian can answer 'what is current test coverage?' from history
Spec validation catches at least one case where implementation diverged from lug spec
child_tasks: lug-qa-guardian-closeout-gate-v1: integrate advisor into closeout protocol as gate owner
lug-qa-guardian-haiku-runner-v1: Haiku sub-agent orchestration for full suite runs
lug-qa-guardian-history-tracker-v1: qa-history.jsonl accumulation and query interface
lug-qa-guardian-spec-validator-v1: validate implementation against Historian spec snapshots
lug-qa-guardian-wakeup-nudge-v1: surface stale coverage warning at session start

_behavior_directive.what_this_is_NOT: A test-writing tool — it orchestrates and tracks, it does not author tests
_behavior_directive.implement_order: Implement after Historian (lug-advisor-historian-v1) for spec validation capability

title: Foundation: Capture environment model (single-env vs multi-env) to drive closeout behavior
summary: Framework foundation should ask what environment model is in place: single-env (prod-only) or multi-env (non-prod + prod). Answer informs closeout routine — multi-env asks if this is a production release; single-env skips the gate but uses a scheduler/counter to decide when to run extra closeout actions.
why_bother: Prevents unnecessary closeout overhead for single-env spokes while preserving production-safety gates for multi-env deployments. Removes ambiguity about when to do a 'full' vs 'quick' closeout commit.
goal: Add env_model field to foundation Q&A; update closeout to branch on single-env vs multi-env; add scheduler/counter for single-env periodic full closeout.
scope: foundation.md Q&A, wai-closeout.md branching logic, WAI-State.json env_model field
constraints: Must be backwards-compatible — existing spokes without env_model default to single-env behavior
